decisions.topic: Storage location and format of declared groups
decisions.decision: Declared groups live in .ros/work/groups.json as {"schema":"praxis.work-groups/1.0.0","groups":[...]}. Each entry is exactly a planner grouping.groups entry (id, members, kind, origin, sharedContext, executionRepository, crossRepository, architectureNotes; fixed field order from PlanningJson.declaredGroupFields) plus store metadata declaredAt (the --occurred-at) and declaredBy (ActorJson actor or null). Groups are kept sorted by ordinal ID. A missing file is an empty store. Writes are temp-file-then-rename and touch nothing else.

decisions.topic: How the planner reads stored groups
decisions.decision: PlanningReadPort gained DeclaredGroups: unit -> Result<DeclaredGroup list,string>; PlanningOperations.gather merges them via GroupDeclaration.mergeInto: configured grouping.groups first, then stored groups in ID order, skipping a stored ID that the --config file also declares (configuration wins). Stored entries are parsed by the same private readDeclaredGroup that parseConfiguration uses for grouping.groups.

decisions.topic: Member state resolution and refusal rules
decisions.decision: GroupDeclaration.memberStates builds Map<id, MemberState> from the backlog queue then overrides with live context (live outranks backlog because a started item keeps its queue entry). Terminal = queue status 'abandoned' or live Complete/Abandoned. Unknown = in neither. create refuses (all reasons reported, fixed order): invalid ID (regex ^GROUP-[A-Z0-9]+(-[A-Z0-9]+)+$), duplicate group ID, no members, repeated member, unknown member, terminal member, crossRepository without executionRepository.

Unified ./ros validate adds WorkGroupCommands.findings (path .ros/work/groups.json): unreadable/malformed store, wrong or missing schema, duplicate IDs, invalid ID, empty members, repeated member, unknown member, cross-repository without repository, empty declaredAt. A member that became terminal after declaration is NOT a finding (PRX-GRP-042 partial completion).

ros work group create --id GROUP-ID --member ITEM [--member ITEM]* --occurred-at TIMESTAMP [--kind KIND] [--origin ORIGIN] [--shared-context TEXT]* [--execution-repository NAME] [--cross-repository] [--architecture-note TEXT]* [--dry-run] [--json] [IDENTITY]. Dispatched in Program.fs through ProvenanceCommands.withResolvedActor. Exit 2 for argument errors, 1 for domain refusal or IO error (nothing written), 0 for recorded or dry-run. --json kinds: group-created (dryRun, recorded, group, members[{id,state}]) and group-rejected (id, recorded:false, errors[]), both with schema praxis.work-groups/1.0.0. Origin defaults to human-declared.

invariants.statement: No work group operation reads or writes a member's lifecycle state: WorkGroupPort's only write is WriteStore (the group store); queue.json and context/current.json are byte-identical before and after create (CLI test).

A stored group entry round-trips through renderGroupStore/parseGroupStore and its declaration fields parse through parseConfiguration's grouping.groups reader to the identical DeclaredGroup; any new declaration field must be added to both readDeclaredGroup and declaredGroupFields.

Planner output for a group stored in the store equals the output for the same group supplied in grouping.groups configuration (equivalence test over PlanningOperations.analyze and Grouping.recommend).
Refusals and --dry-run write nothing (whole-fixture file hash unchanged).
Group IDs are stable and never reused: a duplicate ID is refused rather than overwritten.

reusableAbstractions.name: StoredGroup / GroupStore (GroupStore.empty, add, tryFind, declarations, Schema)

reusableAbstractions.name: GroupDeclaration.memberStates / MemberState
reusableAbstractions.purpose: Each item's own recorded state (live over backlog, Open/Terminal with state code); reuse for show (member states), add (unknown/terminal refusal) and checkpoint (active/completed/remaining).

reusableAbstractions.name: GroupDeclaration.rejections / create / findings / mergeInto, GroupRejection.message
reusableAbstractions.purpose: Pure validation and creation; GroupRejection is the place to add new refusal cases (e.g. AlreadyMember, NotMember, LastMember, RepositoryMismatch).

reusableAbstractions.name: WorkGroupPort, GroupCreateRequest, GroupCreateOutcome, WorkGroupOperations.create/findings
reusableAbstractions.purpose: Application port (ReadStore, Queue, Live, WriteStore) and the read-validate-write pattern with dry-run; extend with add/remove/show operations on the same port.

reusableAbstractions.name: FileWorkGroupStore.read/write/path/declarations
reusableAbstractions.purpose: File IO for .ros/work/groups.json; compiled before FilePlanningRepository so the planner port can read it.

reusableAbstractions.name: FileWorkGroupRepository.create
reusableAbstractions.purpose: File-backed WorkGroupPort composed from FileWorkGroupStore and FilePlanningRepository.readQueue/readLive.

reusableAbstractions.name: PlanningJson.declaredGroupFields, renderGroupStore, parseGroupStore, renderGroupCreated, renderGroupRejected
reusableAbstractions.purpose: JSON contract for stored groups and command results; storedGroupNode (private) renders one stored group and can back a show document.

reusableAbstractions.name: WorkGroupCommands (argument parser, render, findings)
reusableAbstractions.purpose: CLI module for the work group family; flag parsing collects (flag, value) pairs in order. New subcommands go here and are dispatched in Program.fs next to the 'work group create' case (before 'work checkpoint').

reusableAbstractions.purpose: Git fixture with queue (TASK-A, TASK-B ready; TASK-X abandoned) and live context (TASK-DONE complete) plus hash helpers for no-mutation assertions.

unresolvedRisks: The group store write has no lock or journal (temp file then rename only); concurrent group commands could lose an update. Other .ros writers use WorkStateTransaction/BacklogStateTransaction journals.

create does not check members' execution repositories against the group's executionRepository/crossRepository (repository data lives only in planner --config executionRepositories, which create does not read); the planner still warns. PRAXIS-GROUP-03 requires such a check for add.

Node's validate (tools/ros_cli.mjs) does not know groups.json; the F# validate reports group findings only when the file exists, so the differential tests stay equal only while fixtures lack groups.json.
No provenance (./ros provenance record) is recorded for a group itself; declaredBy is the only attribution, and no work event is written for group creation.
The work item description says this must not be merged before EX-ROS-2026-A021 is evaluated and the owner accepts phase two.

constraints: Membership never changes a member's lifecycle state, evidence or attribution (PRX-GRP-002, PRX-GRP-043); keep WorkGroupPort's only write the group store unless a new port is justified.
Keep stored entries in grouping.groups shape; store-only metadata goes beside declaredAt/declaredBy and must be ignored by the planner. Update both readDeclaredGroup and declaredGroupFields together.
Mutating commands need --occurred-at (real current time) and go through ProvenanceCommands.withResolvedActor; --dry-run must write nothing; refusals exit 1 and write nothing; argument errors exit 2.
A member becoming terminal after declaration is partial completion, not a validate finding (PRX-GRP-042).
PRAXIS-GROUP-05 must reuse work checkpoint's durable-checkpoint verification and reference, never replace, members' own checkpoints.
likelyReuse: PRAXIS-GROUP-02 show: GroupStore.tryFind + GroupDeclaration.memberStates for member states; planner's Grouping report (via PlanningOperations.analyze) for planning states, blocked members and progress; render with a storedGroupNode-like JSON; unknown group exits 1.

PRAXIS-GROUP-03 add / PRAXIS-GROUP-04 remove: add GroupRejection cases and pure GroupDeclaration functions, a GroupStore replace/update helper, WorkGroupOperations functions on the same port, and new WorkGroupCommands subcommands; record who added/removed (provenance) probably as per-member metadata in the store entry.
PRAXIS-GROUP-05 checkpoint: CheckpointCommands / FileCheckpointRepository durable verification; member checkpoints are readable from FilePlanningRepository.readLive (PlanningLiveItem.Checkpoint).
WorkGroupTests fixture and fingerprint helpers for no-mutation CLI assertions.
openQuestions: Where should per-member add/remove provenance live: in the stored group entry (e.g. a members metadata list) or as work events in .ros/events/events.jsonl?
Should removing the last member be refused or require an explicit flag (PRAXIS-GROUP-04 allows either)?
Should create (and add) learn execution repositories from the planner configuration to enforce PRX-GRP-051 at write time?
